'''Denis Auroux''' (born April 1977)<ref>{{cite web | title=Denis Auroux - CV | url=https://people.math.harvard.edu/~auroux/cv.html }}</ref> is a French mathematician working in [[geometry]] and [[topology]].

==Education and career==
Auroux was admitted in 1993 to the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)]]. In 1994, he received a [[Licentiate (degree)#France|licentiate]] and ''maîtrise'' in mathematics from [[Paris Diderot University]] (Paris 7). In 1995, he received a licentiate in physics from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (Paris 6) and passed the ''[[agrégation]]''. In 1995, he received a master's degree in mathematics from [[Paris-Sud University]] with a thesis on [[Seiberg–Witten invariants|Seiberg-Witten invariants]] of [[symplectic manifold]]s. In 1999, he received his doctorate from the [[École polytechnique]] with supervisors [[Jean-Pierre Bourguignon]] and [[Michail Leonidowitsch Gromow|Mikhael Gromov]] for a thesis on structure theorems for compact symplectic manifolds via almost-complex techniques.<ref>https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=62981</ref> In 2003, he completed his [[habilitation]] at Paris-Sud University with a thesis on approximately holomorphic techniques and monodromy invariants in symplectic topology. 

As a postdoc, he was a [[C. L. E. Moore instructor|C. L. E. Moore Instructor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1999 to 2002, where he became an assistant professor in 2002, an associate professor in 2004 (tenured in 2006), and a professor in 2009 (on leave from 2009 to 2011). From 2009 to 2018, he was a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. Since Fall 2018, he has been at [[Harvard University]],<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae - Denis Auroux|website=Mathematics Department, Harvard University|url=http://people.math.harvard.edu/~auroux/cv.html}}</ref> where he taught [[Math 55]], two-semester honors undergraduate course on algebra and analysis.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Yefremova |first=Anastasia |date=May 5, 2022 |title=Demystifying Math 55 |url=https://www.math.harvard.edu/demystifying-math-55/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220808194309/https://www.math.harvard.edu/demystifying-math-55/ |archive-date=August 8, 2022 |access-date=August 25, 2022 |website=Department of Mathematics, Harvard University}}</ref>

His research deals with [[symplectic geometry]], [[low-dimensional topology]], and [[Mirror symmetry (string theory)|mirror symmetry]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Denis Auroux|website=Mathematics Department, Harvard University|url=http://people.math.harvard.edu/~auroux/cv.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Denis Auroux - Papers|website=Mathematics Department, Harvard University|url=http://people.math.harvard.edu/~auroux/papers/index.html}} (with links to articles in pdf format)</ref>

In 2002, he received the [[Peccot Lectures|Prix Peccot]] from the [[Collège de France]]. In 2005, he received a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]].<ref name=CV/> He was an invited speaker in 2010 with talk ''Fukaya Categories and bordered Heegaard-Floer Homology''<ref>{{cite book|author=Auroux, D.|year=2010|chapter=Fukaya categories and bordered Heegaard-Floer homology|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians 2010 (ICM 2010)|volume=II|pages=917–941|publisher=Hindustan Book Agency|location=New Delhi|doi=10.1142/9789814324359_0080 |arxiv=1003.2962|isbn=978-981-4324-30-4|s2cid=45582260}}</ref> at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Hyderabad and in 2004 at the European Congress of Mathematicians in Stockholm.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Auroux, Denis|title=Some open questions about symplectic 4-manifolds, singular plane curves, and braid group factorizations|year=2004|eprint=math/0410119 }} (published in 2005 in ''Proceedings of the European Congress of Mathematics: Stockholm, June 27–July 2, 2004'')</ref>

He is also the author of the [[Free and open-source software|free and open-source]] handwritten note-taking software Xournal, which has been developed into Xournal++.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Xournal |url=https://xournal.sourceforge.net/ |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=xournal.sourceforge.net}}</ref>
